reference: She kept throwing the same combination until it felt smooth.
sk: Stále hádzala tú istú kombináciu, kým nešla hladko.
cz: Pořád házela tu samou kombinaci, dokud nešla hladce.
acceptable: She {kept|kept on} {throwing|doing|practising|practicing} the same {combination|combo} until it {felt smooth|went smoothly|flowed smoothly}.

mistakes.text: She kept to throw the same combination until it felt smooth.
mistakes.feedback_sk: Po „keep“ v zmysle „stále robiť“ patrí Gerund: „kept throwing“.
mistakes.feedback_cz: Po „keep“ ve smyslu „pořád dělat“ následuje Gerund: „kept throwing“.
mistakes.feedback_en: When “keep” means “continue”, it is followed by a Gerund: “kept throwing”.

mistakes.text: She kept throw the same combination until it felt smooth.
mistakes.feedback_cz: Po „kept“ je potřeba tvar s „-ing“ (Gerund): „kept throwing“.

mistakes.text: She {was still throwing|still threw} the same combination until it felt smooth.
mistakes.feedback_en: To show she did it again and again, use “kept + -ing”: “kept throwing”.

mistakes.text: She kept throwing the same combination until it {didn't go smoothly|didn't feel smooth}.
mistakes.feedback_sk: Po „until“ nepatrí zápor, hoci slovenčina ho tu má.
mistakes.feedback_cz: Po „until“ nepatří zápor, i když čeština ho tu má.

mistakes.text: She kept throwing the same combination until it felt smoothly.
mistakes.feedback_sk: Po „feel“ patrí prídavné meno, nie príslovka: „felt smooth“.
mistakes.feedback_cz: Po „feel“ následuje přídavné jméno, ne příslovce: „felt smooth“.
mistakes.feedback_en: “Feel” is followed by an adjective, not an adverb: “felt smooth”.

source_issues: SK/CZ say 'until it went smoothly' (nešla hladko / nešla hladce) where EN has 'felt smooth'; both accepted.
